tools.name: verify_claims
tools.description: Fact-check a whole draft or report in one call instead of calling verify_stat once per figure: extract every checkable macro claim from the text — indicator + country + period + claimed value — and submit them together. Each claim gets the same verdict engine as verify_stat (match, close, mismatch,

tools.name: get_series
tools.description: Fetch any supported series by explicit id: 'worldbank/<WDI code>' (needs country), 'imf/<CODE>' (needs country; current-vintage IMF WEO/Fiscal Monitor via the DataMapper API), or 'dbnomics/<PROVIDER>/<DATASET>/<SERIES>' (IMF WEO, OECD, Eurostat and more via DBnomics — dated editions, e.g. 'WEO:2025-

tools.name: search_indicators
tools.description: Search StatCite's curated indicator registry (World Bank WDI + IMF DataMapper/WEO/Fiscal Monitor) by topic — 'inflation', 'debt', 'unemployment', 'poverty' — and discover additional DBnomics datasets. Returns indicator keys usable with get_indicator/verify_stat, with units and source notes.

tools.description: One call for a country's headline economic picture: GDP, GDP growth, GDP per capita, inflation, unemployment, population, current account, trade openness, FDI, life expectancy (World Bank) plus general government debt (IMF DataMapper API, current vintage). Each value carries its own citation. Ideal

tools.name: inflation_adjust
tools.description: Convert a nominal amount between years using official CPI: 'what is 100 (1995) worth in 2025 money?' Works for any country with CPI data (default USA). Returns the adjusted amount, the exact index values and formula used, and the citation. Annual-average precision.

tools.name: fx_convert
tools.description: Convert an amount between currencies using ECB daily reference rates (~30 majors, any date since 1999) or, for ~90 other currencies (BBD, XCD, JMD, KES, …), official annual-average rates from the World Bank — with the method and citations stated explicitly. Pass date='YYYY-MM-DD' for daily or 'YYYY'

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: The official sources behind StatCite (World Bank WDI, IMF WEO & Fiscal Monitor via the IMF DataMapper API — with DBnomics as a vintage-pinned fallback, ECB reference rates, optional FRED), what each covers, its license, and the attribution line to use when citing.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search official economic statistics by free text, e.g. 'inflation barbados' or 'government debt japan'. Returns result ids that can be passed to fetch. Designed for deep-research connectors; for richer control use get_indicator / get_series.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch full data for a result id returned by search (format: 'indicator/<key>/<ISO3>'). Returns the recent observations and the full citation as text.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_indicator · Public sink: verify_claims · Destructive: fetch.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_indicator · Public sink: verify_claims · Destructive: fetch

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_series" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
